target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

The established codebase pattern is to cancel the response body before throwing on non-ok responses (see `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, etc.). This fix applies the same pattern to the Telegram Mini App page handler.

The change is purely mechanical — `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` — following existing codebase convention. The body stream is unread after a non-ok response, so cancelling it is the correct cleanup action with no behavioral side effects.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Resources are cleaned up immediately on auth error instead of dangling until garbage collection.

## Test Results

All 18 tests across 7 test files pass, including the two page-specific tests and the auth-timeout simulation:

```
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.auth-timeout.test.ts (1 test)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.test.ts (6 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/command.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/init-data.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/url.test.ts (3 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/owner.test.ts (2 tests)

 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

## Runtime Evidence Note

This fix is a mechanical change that applies the existing `body?.cancel()` pattern in a single location. Real Telegram Mini App runtime evidence (e.g., confirming the body is cancelled in a live Telegram WebView environment) requires a live Telegram bot setup with Mini App configured, which is not available in the automation pipeline. The change is verified at the code level by:

- Conformance to the established codebase pattern (same idiom used across multiple extensions)
- Unit test coverage (page rendering + auth timeout edge case)
- Static analysis: the `cancel()` call is a no-op when the body is already consumed or null, and `.catch(() => undefined)` prevents unhandled rejections — both standard defensive patterns in this codebase
